name: Brussels sprouts
grown_as: Brussels sprouts, picked from the bottom of the stem up through late autumn and winter. William's records list 'Long Island', a shortish variety.
habit: A single tall, thick, unbranched stem 60 to 90 cm, the sprouts (small tight buds like miniature cabbages) packed in the leaf joints all the way up, topped by a loose rosette of leaves. The lower leaves yellow and drop, leaving the sprouts showing on a bare stem.

leaf.arrangement: Alternate, spiralling up the stem, each with a sprout in its joint
leaf.outline: Rounded to broadly oval, blade 15 to 30 cm, sometimes with a small lobe or two on the stalk
leaf.margin: Wavy, slightly scalloped, no sharp teeth
leaf.veins: A thick pale midrib and strong pale side veins
leaf.surface: Hairless, slightly puckered, with a waxy grey bloom
leaf.colour: Blue-green to grey-green; old lower leaves yellowing

flower.form: A cross-shaped flower of four petals
flower.petals: Four, free, broad and rounded with a long narrow claw, spreading flat
flower.centre: Six stamens, four long and two short, with yellow anthers, round a green style
flower.behind: Four narrow upright green sepals hugging the petal claws
flower.carried: In long, loose spikes on a tall branched stem; the closed buds stay above the open flowers at the top of each spike

fruit: Long, slender pods 5 to 10 cm, cylindrical with slight bumps over the seeds, ending in a short beak 0.5 to 1 cm, spreading upwards along the stems. Green, drying straw-brown and splitting from the bottom to show a pale papery partition. Seeds round, 2 mm, dark red-brown to grey-black.
seedling: Two kidney-shaped seed leaves on short stalks, broader than long with a notch at the tip, like a heart with the stalk at its point, waxy grey-green; the first true leaves oval to round on long stalks, waxy blue-green with wavy edges.
winter: Winter is the crop season: the tall stem stands through frost with sprouts and its leafy top.

leaf: a rounded blade on a long thick pale stalk
waxy blue-green with strong pale veins
bloom: four pale yellow rounded petals in a cross
narrow upright sepals hugging the claws
closed buds above the open flowers
seed: round dark red-brown to grey-black seed 2 mm
seedling: two kidney-shaped seed leaves notched at the tip
young: a single upright stem with long-stalked rounded leaves
crop: a tall single stem packed with small round green sprouts all the way up
a loose rosette of leaves on top
lower stem bare where leaves have dropped, leaf scars showing
flower: sprouts and top opened into many branching flower stems
seedhead: long slender pods with short beaks along tall stems

look_alikes: Kale is tall with frilled or deeply cut leaves and no sprouts. All the cabbage-family crops (cabbage, cauliflower, broccoli, sprouts, kale) are one species and share the waxy blue-green leaf; they differ in what is eaten. Swede and oilseed rape have bluish clasping stem leaves but their young leaves are hairy. Turnip and pak choi (Brassica rapa) have bright yellow flowers held above their buds.
